sections.label: Infrastructure & Utilities
sections.summary: Utility infrastructure lacks comprehensive clearance documentation for overhead lines, transformers, underground utilities, and vertical relationships; missing elevation surveys, dimension callouts, and equipment specifications.

sections.label: Street Trees & Landscaping
sections.summary: Landscape plan lacks species identification, clearance specifications, and electrical infrastructure overlay; Austin Energy approval missing for trees in transmission line easements.

sections.label: Street Frontage & Pedestrian Circulation
sections.summary: Driveway clearances and crossing specifications, as well as site feature clearances, lack documentation.

sections.label: Plan Documentation & Administrative
sections.summary: Easement conflicts and private property compliance are unverified; construction contractor notification and staging documentation are missing.

comments.headline: Missing building elevations and clearance surveys
comments.summary: No building elevation sheets, section/plan dimension exhibits, or registered surveyor mid-span clearance survey data are provided. Required documentation prevents verification of 7.5-foot and 15-foot clearance compliance for overhead electric facilities throughout the site.

details.text: No building elevation sheets showing surveyed overhead conductor elevations and clearance dimension annotations are included in the site plan package. Building elevation sheets are required per UCM § 1.10.3 but are absent.

runComments.comment: Overhead electric lines exist on or adjacent to site. No building elevation sheets with surveyed overhead conductor elevations and clearance dimension annotations are included in the site plan package. Required building elevation sheets showing conductor heights and clearances to building features are missing.
Building elevation sheets with surveyed conductor elevations are not included in the submitted site plan set.

No building elevation sheets are included in the site plan set showing surveyed elevations and locations of overhead conductors. Building elevation sheets with surveyed conductor data and clearance dimension annotations are required per UCM § 1.10.3 to demonstrate that required clearances are met.

details.text: Section and plan view exhibits showing dimensions from the outermost electric conductor to building edges and projections are not provided. Required clearance verification exhibits are missing from the site plan package.

runComments.comment: Section and plan view exhibits showing dimensions from outer electric conductor to outermost edge of buildings and building projections are not provided. Required clearance verification exhibits are missing from the site plan package.
No section or plan view exhibits provided showing dimension lines from outer conductor to building edges.

Plans do not include section and plan view exhibits showing dimensions from the outer electric conductor to the outermost edge of buildings, building projections, retaining walls, or other site features. Clearance verification requires dimension lines extending from the outside conductor to all structures and site improvements.

details.text: No registered surveyor's mid-span clearance survey data is provided documenting overhead conductor elevations and pole locations. When vertical clearance appears marginal, surveyor data is required but not submitted.

runComments.comment: Proposed driveway finished surface elevations are shown on the grading plan. Overhead electric lines exist on site boundaries with spot elevations shown on electrical plan. However, no registered surveyor's mid-span clearance survey data is provided, and no profile sections show vertical clearances from overhead line lowest point to driveway surfaces. When vertical clearance appears marginal or insufficient, surveyor data is required but not submitted.
No registered surveyor mid-span clearance survey provided showing pole locations and conductor elevations for clearance verification.

Driveway proposed grades (Sheet 11: 679.75-688.40 feet) are shown in proximity to overhead electric facilities. The vertical clearance from these grades to the overhead conductors is not documented. A registered surveyor's mid-span clearance survey is required to verify that minimum clearance requirements (16-18 feet for driveways per UCM § 1.10.6.2) are satisfied, but no such survey data is provided.

comments.headline: Buildings and structures lack overhead line clearance verification
comments.summary: Proposed buildings and elevated structures are positioned in proximity to overhead electric lines without documented clearance verification. No elevations or dimensions demonstrate compliance with required 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground and 15-foot radial clearances from the outside conductor.
comments.crossDep: Electrical utility coordination may be required if structures must be relocated or overhead electric line repositioned.
comments.attn: Buildings 6, 7, 8 specifically noted near southern OHE line; all buildings near western OHE line on Valley View Road ROW. Confirm whether pole relocation is proposed or structures must be repositioned.

details.text: Buildings are shown in plan view relative to overhead electric lines but no surveyed building elevations are provided to verify required 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance from the outside conductor. Clearance cannot be verified without elevation views dimensioned from the conductor.

runComments.comment: Overhead electric lines exist on western and southern site boundaries; buildings are set back from these lines on plan view, but no surveyed building elevations provided showing conductor heights or clearance dimensions. Cannot verify 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance without elevation views dimensioned from the outside conductor.
Buildings 6, 7, and 8 are shown in proximity to the southern OHE line without any documented clearance dimensions from the outside conductor. No clearance verification provided.

Buildings are shown in plan view relative to overhead electric lines on Sheet 9, but no building elevation sheets with surveyed overhead conductor elevations are provided to verify the required 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance from the outside conductor.

details.text: Buildings maintain apparent setbacks from property lines on plan, but no surveyed elevations or clearance dimensions verify 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground and 15-foot radial clearances as permanent requirements. Buildings 7 and 8 adjacent to southern OHE; all buildings near western OHE line.

runComments.comment: Overhead electric lines exist in right-of-way adjacent to site (western and southern boundaries); buildings maintain apparent setbacks from property lines, but no surveyed elevations or clearance dimensions verify 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground and 15-foot radial clearances as permanent requirements per UCM § 1.10.3.
Buildings located near OHE lines on south and east boundaries but no clearance dimensions from conductor shown on site plan.

Overhead electric lines exist along the western property line (Valley View Road) and southern property line, with poles and conductors visible on the existing conditions survey (Sheet 4). Buildings 7 and 8 are located adjacent to the southern OHE line boundary, and the western driveway crosses underneath the western OHE line. No surveyed elevations and clearance dimensions are provided to demonstrate that buildings maintain the required 7.5-foot sky-to-ground and 15-foot radial clearances from the outside conductors.

details.text: Building projections (overhangs, awnings, balconies, decks, roofs, patios) are not shown in elevation view with dimensions to overhead conductors. Building elevation and section views required to verify clearances are not provided.

runComments.comment: No building projections (overhangs, awnings, balconies, decks, roofs, patios) are shown in elevation view with dimensions to overhead electric conductors. Building elevation and section views required to verify clearances are not provided in the site plan package.
No building elevation sheets provided showing surveyed conductor elevations and clearances from building projections (overhangs, balconies, canopies) to overhead conductors.

No building elevation sheets showing projected building elements (overhangs, awnings, balconies, decks, roofs, patios) relative to overhead conductors are provided to verify clearances. Applicant must provide surveyed building elevations with conductor locations.

details.text: Elevated walkways and pedestrian platforms are shown on site plan but no clearance dimensions from OHE lines are provided. No elevation or section drawings verify required 15-foot radial clearance.

runComments.comment: Elevated walkways and pedestrian platforms are shown on site plan but no clearance dimensions from OHE lines are provided.

Sheet 9 shows the overall site layout with various walkways and potential elevated structures, but no elevation or section drawings are provided to verify that stairs, elevated walkways, or platforms maintain the required 15-foot radial clearance from overhead electric distribution facilities.

details.text: Emergency access structures (elevated platforms or bridges) are not explicitly identified on the site plan. If present, section views showing required clearances from overhead conductors are not provided.

runComments.comment: Emergency access structures not clearly identified on plans. No elevation sections provided.

No emergency access bridges or elevated platforms are explicitly identified on the site plan. If such structures exist as part of the site design, section views showing the required clearances from overhead conductors are not provided.

details.text: Vehicle parking areas are shown on site plan but site plan does not explicitly identify vehicle display pads or document vertical clearance dimensions for any parking areas in proximity to OHE.

runComments.comment: Parking locations shown but no vertical clearance from OHE lines documented.

Vehicle parking areas are shown on the site plan (both surface and garage parking), but the site plan does not explicitly identify any vehicle display pads or indicate which parking areas (if any) are positioned beneath overhead electric lines. Vertical clearance dimensions are not provided for any parking areas in proximity to OHE.

comments.headline: Structures in utility easements lack clearance verification
comments.summary: Buildings, driveways, and retaining walls are positioned within electric utility easements or adjacent property-line areas without documented clearance from outside conductors or utility access space. 5-foot easements along boundaries cannot accommodate customer facilities.
comments.crossDep: Austin Energy input required to confirm easement boundaries, permissions, and whether structures can be relocated or easement modified.
comments.attn: Existing 5-foot electric easements shown along property boundaries. Confirm whether proposed site features (buildings, walls, driveways) actually encroach into easement, or if there is adequate clearance from easement edge.

details.text: Existing conditions survey shows 5-foot electric easements along property boundaries and overhead distribution facilities through/adjacent to property. Proposed site features on Sheet 9 (buildings, driveways, retaining walls) located in proximity to easements and OHE lines. No dimension exhibits verify minimum 7.5-foot clearance from outside conductor nor confirm features do not violate absolute prohibition on customer facilities under/over distribution lines.

runComments.comment: Sheet 2 (Plat) and Sheet 21 show electric easements on site boundaries and interior. Buildings and site features are located throughout the site, including within and adjacent to easement areas. However, no clearance dimensions verify that customer facilities within electric easements maintain minimum 7.5-foot clearance from outside conductors. Furthermore, the absolute prohibition on installing customer facilities under or over Austin Energy distribution facilities cannot be verified without complete easement delineation on all relevant sheets.
Driveway and retaining walls shown directly over/crossing OHE line, violating absolute prohibition on customer facilities under/over distribution lines. No clearance documentation provided.

The existing conditions survey (Sheet 4) shows 5-foot electric easements along property boundaries and overhead electric lines running through/adjacent to the property. The proposed site features (buildings, driveways, retaining walls) shown on Sheet 9 are located in proximity to these easements and overhead lines. However, no dimension exhibits verify that items within the electric easements or beneath overhead distribution lines maintain the minimum 7.5-foot clearance from the outside conductor. The absolute prohibition against installing customer facilities under or over distribution lines cannot be verified as being met.

details.text: Buildings shown on site plan are setback from property lines, but exact distances from permanent structure foundations to property lines are not clearly dimensioned. Without precise setback dimensions and clear delineation of utility facility locations in adjacent ROW, cannot verify adequate clearance space exists for future utility work.

runComments.comment: Buildings shown on site plan are setback from property lines, but exact distances from permanent structure foundations to property lines are not clearly dimensioned. Without precise setback dimensions and without clear delineation of where electric facilities are located in adjacent ROW or neighboring properties, cannot verify that adequate clearance space exists for future utility work.
Building setbacks from property line not explicitly dimensioned on site plan.

While buildings are shown on the site plan (Sheet 9), no building foundation detail drawings are provided, and no explicit documentation shows whether foundations are located within 5 feet of the property line where electric facilities in the right-of-way or adjacent property require clearance space.

details.text: Down guy anchor locations from distribution poles not explicitly shown or dimensioned on site plan or easement exhibits. No easement exhibit showing 10-foot width extending 5 feet past the anchor ground entry point is provided on submitted site plan.

runComments.comment: Down guy anchors from distribution poles (if they exist on site) are not explicitly shown or dimensioned on the site plan or easement exhibit (Plat, Sheet 2). Cannot verify whether dedicated easements for down guy anchors (10-foot width, 5-foot minimum extension past anchor ground entry) are provided or properly dimensioned.
Down guy anchor locations and associated easement boundaries not shown on site plan.

The existing conditions survey (Sheet 4) identifies down guy locations but does not clearly show the specific anchor point locations or provide easement boundaries. No easement exhibit showing 10-foot width extending 5 feet past the anchor ground entry point is provided on the submitted site plan.

details.text: Electrical design plan shows underground electric infrastructure but does not clearly indicate whether new power poles are proposed for underground service conversion. If poles are proposed, their horizontal spacing relative to existing poles is not documented with required 20-foot minimum dimension.

runComments.comment: The electrical design plan (Sheet 21) shows underground electric infrastructure but does not clearly indicate whether new power poles are proposed for the underground service conversion. If new poles are proposed, their horizontal spacing relative to existing poles is not documented with the required 20-foot minimum dimension.

comments.headline: No clearance dimension callouts shown on site plans
comments.summary: The site plan provides no clearance dimensions at all from overhead electric facilities to site features. When dimensions are absent, measurement origin (outside conductor vs. pole centerline) cannot be verified. Per UCM § 1.10.3, critical measurement must originate from outside conductor.
comments.attn: This is a foundational documentation gap affecting verification of nearly all other clearance items. All clearance dimension callouts must show measurement origin from the outside/outermost conductor, not from pole centerline.

details.text: Site plan sheets show no clearance dimension callouts originating from overhead electric conductor locations to any site features (buildings, structures, equipment, driveways, walls, fences). Complete absence of dimensions prevents verification that measurements originate from outside conductor per UCM § 1.10.3 requirement.

runComments.comment: Clearance dimensions required by code are not shown on site plan sheets. Where clearance dimensions are lacking, no verification can be performed that they extend from the outside conductor (not pole centerline or pole structure). The requirement that dimensions originate from the outer conductor, not pole center, cannot be verified when dimensions are absent.
No clearance dimensions shown on any plan sheets. Measurement methodology (from outside conductor vs. pole center) cannot be verified.

The site plan provides no clearance dimensions at all from any overhead electric facilities to site features. Where dimensions are absent, it is impossible to verify that they are measured from the outside conductor rather than from pole centerline. Per UCM § 1.10.3, the critical measurement point is the outside conductor, not the pole centerline. The plan's complete absence of clearance dimensions means this requirement cannot be evaluated.

comments.headline: Underground utility clearances undimensioned
comments.summary: Multiple underground utility lines (water, wastewater, storm drain, electric) are shown in proximity to transformer pads, but no horizontal or vertical separation dimensions are labeled. The 5-foot minimum clearance from water, wastewater, and storm drain, and 12-inch clearance from electric lines cannot be verified. Storm drain at Pad 3 shows possible critical violation.
comments.crossDep: Stormwater/Drainage (Pad 3 storm drain conflict resolution); Water/Wastewater utilities (line routing coordination)
comments.attn: CRITICAL: Pad 3 storm drain conflict requires immediate verification via profile section or measurement. Vision analysis indicates clearance may be <5 feet or zero. All utility clearances must be dimensioned on electrical plan or utility profile sheets. Provide horizontal and vertical separations for each utility line near each pad.

details.text: Water lines shown on Utility Tap Plan (Sheet 19) and Electrical Plan (Sheet 21) near all transformer pad locations, but no horizontal clearance dimensions labeled between pad edges and water line locations. Minimum 5-foot horizontal clearance per UCM § 2.9.1.B.2 cannot be verified.

runComments.comment: Water lines (W) are shown on Sheet 21 near all transformer pads, and on Sheet 19 (Utility Tap Plan). However, no specific horizontal clearance dimensions are labeled between pad edges and water line locations. Measurement tool would be appropriate for verification if visual dimensions are insufficient.

Utility Tap Plan (Sheet 19) shows water line routing through the site, but clearance dimensions between water lines and transformer pads are not marked. The minimum 5-foot horizontal clearance from water lines cannot be verified without marked dimensions on the electrical or utility plan.
Water lines shown on utility plan in proximity to transformer pads but clearance dimensions not provided. Minimum 5-foot horizontal clearance not verifiable.

details.text: Wastewater lines shown on Utility Tap Plan and Electrical Plan near transformer pad locations (notably TP3 with WW line ~5–10 feet away west side), but no horizontal clearance dimensions labeled. Minimum 5-foot horizontal clearance per UCM § 2.9.1.B.2 cannot be verified.

runComments.comment: Wastewater lines (WW) are shown on Sheet 21 near transformer pad locations, particularly TP3 which has a WW line running approximately 5-10 feet away on the west side. However, no specific horizontal clearance dimensions are labeled.

Utility Tap Plan (Sheet 19) shows wastewater line routing through the site, but clearance dimensions between wastewater lines and transformer pads are not marked. The minimum 5-foot horizontal clearance from wastewater lines cannot be verified without marked dimensions.
Wastewater lines shown on utility plan in proximity to transformer pads but clearance dimensions not provided. Minimum 5-foot horizontal clearance not verifiable.

details.text: Storm drain line on Sheet 21 runs directly through corridor between Buildings 4 and 5 where Transformer Pad 3 is located. Vision analysis indicates storm drain passes extremely close to or directly underneath pad with clearance visually estimated <5 feet, possibly zero. No separation dimensions shown; no profile view provided. Run 1 flagged as definitive failure. This represents critical violation requiring immediate resolution.

runComments.comment: Sheet 21 shows a storm drain line (SD) running directly through the corridor between Buildings 4 and 5 where Transformer Pad 3 is located. Vision analysis indicates the storm drain line passes extremely close to, or potentially directly underneath, the transformer pad symbol (clearance visually estimated at < 5 feet). No separation dimensions are shown. No profile view is provided demonstrating clearance. This represents a clear violation of the minimum 5-foot horizontal clearance requirement.

Storm Sewer Plan (Sheet 12) and Electrical Plan (Sheet 21) show storm drain and transformer locations, but clearance dimensions between storm drain lines and transformer pads are not marked. The minimum 5-foot horizontal clearance cannot be verified without marked dimensions.
Storm drain lines shown on both storm sewer and electrical plans in close proximity to transformer pads but clearance dimensions not provided. Minimum 5-foot horizontal clearance not verifiable.

details.text: Multiple underground utilities shown near transformer pads (electric, water, wastewater, storm drain lines), but no specific horizontal or vertical separation dimensions labeled on any plan or profile sheet. Minimum 12-inch horizontal and vertical clearance from other underground utilities per UCM § 1.10.5.A cannot be verified without profile views or dimensioned separation callouts.

runComments.comment: Multiple underground utilities are shown near transformer pads (electric lines, water lines, wastewater lines, storm drain lines), but no specific separation dimensions (horizontal or vertical) are labeled on any plan or profile sheet. The minimum 12-inch horizontal and vertical clearance from other underground utilities cannot be verified without profile views or dimensioned separation callouts.

Utility plans show water, wastewater, and storm drain lines, but specific horizontal and vertical clearance dimensions between transformer pads and underground utilities are not marked. The 12-inch minimum horizontal and vertical clearance from other underground utilities cannot be verified without marked dimensions or utility profile/detail sheets.
Multiple utilities shown in proximity to transformer pads but 12-inch horizontal and vertical clearances not dimensioned. Compliance not verifiable.

comments.headline: Transformer equipment and service specifications missing
comments.summary: Electrical specifications do not identify transformer type (oil-filled vs. dry-type), service configuration (standard vs. niche), service type (single vs. three-phase), or gas utility service presence. Multiple clearance, design, and documentation requirements are contingent on these specifications and cannot be verified.
comments.crossDep: Architectural (fire rating for niche service); Utility company (gas service confirmation)
comments.attn: Equipment/service specifications must be confirmed from electrical designer and cross-checked against AE Design requirements document.

details.text: Transformer type (oil-filled vs. dry-type) not specified on electrical plan. Window, door, and ventilating duct clearance requirements (12 feet if oil-filled and <5-foot lateral separation; 10 feet otherwise) vary by type and cannot be verified.

runComments.comment: No window, door, or ventilating duct locations are dimensioned relative to transformer pads. The requirement applies to oil-filled equipment when windows/doors/ducts are less than 12 feet from grade or lack 5-foot lateral separation; however, transformer type (oil-filled vs. dry-type) is not specified on the plans.

Electrical specifications do not identify any transformers as oil-filled equipment. Building elevations showing windows, doors, and ventilating ducts with grade elevations and lateral clearance dimensions are not provided. Without transformer type confirmation and detailed elevation information, 12-foot horizontal clearance requirement cannot be verified.
Transformer equipment specifications (oil-filled vs. dry-type) and building elevations showing window/door locations not provided. 12-foot clearance requirement from windows/doors cannot be verified.

details.text: Transformer type (oil-filled vs. dry-type) not specified. Liquid drainage direction requirement (away from buildings) applies only to oil-filled equipment and cannot be verified without equipment type confirmation.

runComments.comment: The requirement applies specifically to oil-filled equipment—liquid flow must be directed away from buildings. Transformer type (oil-filled vs. dry-type) is not specified on the electrical plan. General grading analysis on Sheet 11 suggests drainage slopes direct flow away from buildings in the areas where transformers are located, but specific confirmation of transformer type and pad-level grading is not documented.

Electrical specifications do not identify whether any transformers are oil-filled equipment. Grading and Drainage Plan (Sheet 11) does not show surface flow direction or grading slopes specifically around transformer pad locations. Without confirmation of oil-filled equipment type and documentation of drainage direction away from buildings, compliance with liquid-flow-away-from-building requirement cannot be verified.
Transformer equipment type (oil-filled vs. dry-type) not specified on electrical plan. Drainage direction requirement for oil-filled equipment cannot be verified.

details.text: Fire escapes and stairwells are not identified or shown on electrical plan or fire protection plan adjacent to transformer pad locations. Fire escape clearance requirement (20 feet for oil-filled equipment only) cannot be verified without fire escape documentation and equipment type confirmation.

runComments.comment: Stairwells and fire escapes are not shown on the electrical or fire protection plans in proximity to transformer pads. Fire Protection Plan (Sheet 10) shows fire lanes and hydrants but does not identify stairwells or fire escapes adjacent to transformer locations. Compliance cannot be verified from available documentation.

details.text: Fire escape clearance (minimum 20 feet) is required only if transformers are oil-filled equipment. Equipment type not documented on electrical specifications, so fire escape clearance requirement applicability and compliance cannot be verified.

runComments.comment: Electrical specifications do not confirm whether any transformers are oil-filled. Building elevations or sections showing fire escape locations in relation to transformer pads are not provided. The 20-foot fire escape clearance requirement applies only to oil-filled equipment and cannot be verified without equipment type confirmation and fire escape location documentation.

Fire hydrant location shown on Fire Protection Plan but clearance dimension from transformer pad not provided. 20-foot requirement for oil-filled equipment cannot be verified without equipment specifications and dimensions.

details.text: Gas utility service presence not documented on site/utility plans. If gas service is proposed, horizontal clearance of 24 inches (<60 psi) or 36 inches (≥60 psi) from gas lines is required but cannot be verified without confirming gas service presence.

runComments.comment: Site plans do not show gas utility infrastructure or identify whether gas service is proposed to the site. Utility Plan (Sheet 19) legend does not include gas line symbols or routing. Compliance with 24-inch (pressures <60 psi) or 36-inch (pressures ≥60 psi) clearance from gas lines cannot be evaluated without confirmation of gas service presence and pipeline locations.

details.text: If Transformer Pad 3 within the Vault Easement represents a niche service installation, 35-foot minimum vertical clearance requirement inside niche and niche entrance applies. Cross-section drawings demonstrating this clearance are not provided; niche service configuration not confirmed.

runComments.comment: Transformer Pad 3 is located within a Vault Easement boundary per electrical plan notation. If this constitutes a niche service (equipment within building-like footprint, accessible from outside), a minimum 35-foot vertical clearance is required inside the niche and niche entrance. Cross-section drawings demonstrating this clearance are not provided. The presence of a niche configuration and its clearance compliance cannot be verified.

details.text: If Pad 3 within Vault Easement is a niche service installation, 3-hour fire wall rating for walls and ceilings, ventilation system specifications, and Austin Energy Design business unit consultation documentation are required but not visible in submitted documentation.

runComments.comment: If Transformer Pad 3 within the Vault Easement represents a niche service installation, architectural specifications showing 3-hour fire wall rating for walls and ceilings, ventilation system specifications, and documentation of Austin Energy Design business unit consultation are required. These specifications and approvals are not visible in the submitted electrical, architectural, or specification documentation.

details.text: Transformer pad dimensions (length × width × depth) not specified on electrical plan. Service type (single-phase or three-phase) not identified. No reference to AE Design-approved transformer pad detail sheets for specified service type provided in construction documents.

runComments.comment: Sheet 21 shows four transformer pads labeled as 'Electrical Transformer Pad' but provides NO dimensions specifying pad size (length × width × depth). The requirement mandates that transformer pad dimensions match Austin Energy Design-approved transformer pad detail sheets for the specified service type (single-phase or three-phase). No pad dimensions are provided on the plans, and no reference to Austin Energy Design detail sheets or service type specifications is documented. This is a critical omission.

Transformer pad dimensions are not specified or shown on the electrical plan. Service type (single-phase or three-phase) is not identified for any transformer. AE Design-approved transformer pad detail sheets for the specified service type are not included in the submitted documentation. Pad dimensions must match AE Design standards for the intended service configuration, and details are required for construction compliance.

Transformer pad dimensions not shown on electrical plan. No reference to Austin Energy Design-approved transformer pad detail sheets for specified service type (single-phase or three-phase). Pad sizing and specifications not verifiable.

comments.headline: Electrical Infrastructure Not Overlaid on Landscape Plan
comments.summary: Electrical plan (Sheet 21) shows utility poles, transformer pads, underground lines, and pull boxes. Landscape plan (Sheet 31) does not depict or reference this infrastructure. Without overlays, tree clearance and root barrier requirements cannot be verified.
comments.crossDep: Electrical design team and Austin Energy to confirm equipment locations and access requirements for landscape plan overlay

details.text: Utility poles are not marked or identified on landscape plan (Sheet 31). While OHE line is shown, specific pole locations are not distinctly labeled. Measured clearances from trees to poles (10-foot minimum per UCM § 1.10.10.4) cannot be verified without pole locations.

runComments.comment: Utility poles are not clearly marked or identified on the landscape plan (Sheet 31). While the overhead electric (OHE) line is shown along the western boundary, specific pole locations are not distinctly labeled. Without clear pole identification, clearances from proposed trees cannot be verified.

Compliance with the 10-foot utility pole clearance requirement cannot be verified because utility poles are not shown on the landscape plan (Sheet 31). Vision analysis confirmed that the OHE line is depicted but no pole locations or symbols are visible on the landscape plan. The electrical design plan (Sheet 21) notes an existing OHE line on the western edge outside the property boundary, but does not show pole locations within or adjacent to the development site. Applicant must provide: (1) identification of all existing and proposed overhead electric utility pole locations shown on site plan or utility plan; (2) landscape plan showing pole locations if any exist within or adjacent to development site; (3) measured clearances from trees to pole centers if poles are present.

Landscape plan and electrical plan (Sheet 21) do not show utility pole locations explicitly marked or dimensioned. While overhead electric lines are depicted on the landscape plan, specific pole locations are not identified on either sheet, preventing verification of 10-foot clearance requirement from poles.

details.text: Five transformer pads with vault easements identified on electrical design plan (Sheet 21) are absent from landscape plan (Sheet 31). Trees may be proposed within 10 lateral feet of pad-mounted equipment. Clearances from pad perimeters and access doors to trees cannot be dimensioned without transformer pad locations shown on landscape plan.

runComments.comment: The electrical design plan (Sheet 21) identifies five transformer pads with vault easements. None of these transformer pad locations are shown on the landscape plan (Sheet 31). UCM § 1.10.10.4 requires trees to remain ≥10 lateral feet from pad-mounted equipment; without transformer pad locations visible on the landscape plan, clearances cannot be verified or demonstrated.

Trees may be proposed within 10 lateral feet of the transformer pad (pad-mounted electric equipment) shown on Sheet 9 near the western site boundary between Building 2 and Valley View Road. Vision analysis of the landscape plan (Sheet 31) indicates trees in close proximity to a 'rectangular pad structure' in this area. However, compliance cannot be verified because: (1) clearance distances from the transformer pad to tree trunks are not dimensioned on the landscape plan; (2) the exact location and footprint of the transformer pad is not referenced or dimensioned on the landscape plan; (3) no notation indicates access door orientation for pad-mounted equipment. Applicant must provide: (1) transformer pad location and footprint clearly marked on landscape plan with dimensions; (2) measured clearance distances from pad perimeter (and access door area if applicable) to each tree within 25 feet; (3) verification of 10-foot minimum clearance.

Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows transformer pads and electrical infrastructure with underground distribution, but the landscape plan (Sheet 31) does not clearly identify pad-mounted equipment locations or access door orientations in relation to proposed trees. Without explicit pad-mount locations on the landscape plan, the 10-foot clearance requirement cannot be verified.

details.text: Extensive underground electrical conduits, pull boxes, and vault easements shown on electrical plan (Sheet 21) are not depicted on landscape plan (Sheet 31). Trees are distributed throughout site above underground infrastructure. Clearances of ≥5 feet from underground equipment per UCM § 1.10.10.4 cannot be verified without underground utility locations overlaid on landscape plan.

runComments.comment: The electrical design plan (Sheet 21) shows extensive underground electrical conduits, pull boxes, and vault easements. The landscape plan (Sheet 31) does not depict underground electrical lines, pull boxes, or vaults. UCM § 1.10.10.4 requires trees remain ≥5 lateral feet from underground electric equipment. Without underground utility locations shown on the landscape plan, clearances cannot be verified.

Trees are proposed throughout the site where underground electrical infrastructure (transformers, pull boxes, service lines) exists. Per Sheet 21, multiple underground transformer pads and pull boxes are located throughout the development serving each building. Sheet 31 shows trees distributed around the perimeter and near buildings, but clearance distances from underground equipment to tree locations are not dimensioned. The 5-foot minimum clearance requirement cannot be verified because: (1) underground equipment locations are not cross-referenced or overlay on the landscape plan; (2) no clearance dimensions are provided; (3) tree symbol locations cannot be precisely related to underground utility coordinates. Applicant must provide: (1) overlay of underground electric equipment locations (transformer pads, pull boxes) on landscape plan with coordinates; (2) measured clearance distances from each tree to nearest underground equipment; (3) verification that all trees maintain minimum 5-foot lateral clearance from underground equipment.

Sheet 21 (Electrical Plan) shows underground electric lines and pull boxes, but the landscape plan (Sheet 31) does not overlay underground equipment locations with sufficient clarity to verify 5-foot clearance from tree planting locations. Coordination between electrical and landscape plans is insufficient for verification.

details.text: Trees proposed within 20 lateral feet of underground electric equipment require 4-foot deep root barriers positioned 5 feet from equipment per UCM § 1.10.10.4. Without underground equipment locations shown on landscape plan, trees within the 20-foot clearance zone cannot be identified. Landscape details (Sheet 37) do not specify root barrier installation requirements or locations.

runComments.comment: UCM § 1.10.10.4 requires trees within 20 lateral feet of underground electric equipment to have root barriers (minimum 4 feet deep, positioned 5 feet from equipment). Underground electrical equipment is not shown on the landscape plan (Sheet 31), so which trees (if any) fall within the 20-foot zone cannot be determined. Additionally, no root barrier details are provided on the landscape plan.

Root barriers (minimum 4 feet deep, positioned 5 feet from equipment) are required for trees proposed within 20 lateral feet of underground electric equipment. Compliance cannot be verified for multiple reasons: (1) underground equipment locations are not clearly mapped on the landscape plan (see EL-2.8); (2) no clearance dimensions identify which trees are within the 20-foot zone; (3) landscape plan details and notes do not specify root barrier requirements or details; (4) tree locations cannot be precisely measured against underground equipment coordinates. Applicant must provide: (1) landscape plan identifying which trees are within 20 feet of underground equipment; (2) specification notes requiring 4-foot deep root barriers positioned 5 feet from equipment for affected trees; (3) landscape details showing root barrier installation specifications; (4) measured clearances documenting placement.

Landscape details (Sheet 37) and landscape plan (Sheet 31) do not show explicit root barrier specifications at trees planted near underground electric facilities. The landscape plan does not clearly identify which trees are within 20-foot clearance zone of underground equipment, and landscape details do not specify root barrier requirements (minimum 4 feet deep, positioned 5 feet from equipment).

comments.headline: Austin Energy Approval Missing for Trees in Restricted Clearance Zones
comments.summary: Three mitigation trees in southeast corner are positioned 2–5 feet from the OHE line, placing them within prohibited clearance zones (15 feet for non-utility-compatible distribution trees; 25 feet for large distribution trees; 50 feet for transmission). No written Austin Energy approval documentation is evident.
comments.crossDep: Austin Energy must review and approve any trees proposed within restricted clearance zones per UCM § 1.10.10.3
